_comment: THE ARTIFACT FLOOR for /skill-builder -- the six rows ratified by the owner 2026-08-08 (F2.5.1).
Source of every clause: state/projects/skill-builder/records/2026-08-07-artifact-floor-six-rows.md
WHAT THIS GRADES: the RUN-EVIDENCE file a single pass through the chain leaves behind --
one file, six '## BUILDER PHASE N' sections. phase_gate.py slices to the phase's own
section (never the cumulative file) and checks that phase's requires/forbids.
WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* GRADE: the six phase DRIVER files in phases/. Their step lists are
L7/L14 HARD-locked -- 'Only the human may change it' -- so nothing here touches them.
THE BOUND, ADOPTED NOT RE-LITIGATED (phase_gate.py's own DECLARED UNCHECKABLE block):
a 'requires' pattern check proves the declared text is PRESENT in the phase's own slice.
It CANNOT prove the matched text is real work -- 'no trace independent of the artifact
exists'. That is TERMINAL; do not try to fix it with a substantive-content heuristic
(built, measured and REVERTED already). So every phase below ALSO requires its own
INDEPENDENT TRACE field -- a value the phase could not have written by itself (a git
hash, a foreign session id, a fan-out return count). THAT is the causation half.
'forbids' is NOT covered by the bound and stays sound as built.
SCHEMA NOTE, learned by running it 2026-08-08: 'requires' entries take a bare {id,
pattern}. 'forbids' entries are delegated whole to forbidden_content.py and take
{id, mode, term|pattern} -- mode 'declaration' (a labelled assignment) or 'mention' (any
word-boundary hit) or 'regex' (explicit pattern, required for anything the other two
do not cover). Every forbids rule below is mode 'regex' because each targets a
field-value shape, not a bare term. Mixing the two schemas returns CANNOT EVALUATE --
fail-closed, which is correct behaviour and is how this note got written.
RANKED BY HOW REAL THE GATE IS (from F2.5.1): phase 5 (git hash) and phase 6 (foreign
session id) are strongest -- neither can be produced by the phase that claims them.
Phase 1 is WEAKEST and is deliberately NOT sold as gated: two of its three done-clauses
are human_in_the_loop and no independent trace exists. Recorded, not smoothed.

1.name: define the desired outcome  [WEAKEST -- see _comment]
1._tag: human_in_the_loop on clauses (a) and (b); enforceable on clause (c) only
1._independent_trace: NONE. The same session writes both the brief and its own arm row.

requires.why: closed set, LAW 1. Step 1.7 legitimately writes NO brief for a one-step skill, so absence of a brief is a legal outcome -- but the DECISION must be recorded either way.
the arm-events.log row citation. Weak (same session writes it) -- it proves an output exists, never that the phase happened.

forbids.why: the no-outcome member must break loudly, never pass silently

2.name: propose the phases + each phase's desired outcome
2._independent_trace: the human's raw answer at fork 2.6, captured verbatim by fork.py

requires.why: step 2.9: 'Record, for each phase, whether its done is the human's own words or a machine draft the human accepted.' Closed set.
the phase cannot close on anything but B; this is the independent trace

forbids.why: a builder-drafted outcome the human never saw is 'a guess wearing a locked outcome's clothes' (driver stop-check)

3.name: decide the steps  [STRONGEST STRUCTURAL -- every clause is a field check]
3._independent_trace: the denominator comes from BUILDER PHASE 2's artifact -- this phase cannot set its own bar (LAW 4.1: pin the denominator first)

requires.why: LAW 4.1 -- completeness is permanently a native-id set-diff in code, never a model's judgement
the denominator must be traceable to the PRIOR phase, or completeness is asserted not proven
every step carries purpose + actor + layer; every human step declares LLM or CODE with a valid-answer set and a failure mode

forbids.why: a phase that silently lost its step list must refuse, not report clean
a step missing its actor, layer, or (for a CODE step) its valid-answer set and failure mode

4.name: the tension swarm
4._independent_trace: four separate subagent processes -- a skipped swarm has no returns to capture

requires.why: LAW 4.1 -- fire the check AT THE FAN-OUT RETURN BOUNDARY, never at phase exit, where the drop is already invisible
step 4.10 -- 'the rejections matter as much as the fixes; an unrecorded rejection gets re-proposed by the next reader who looks'
step 4.5 -- 'nothing is thrown away'. map_carry_receipt.py proves every finding reached the record or was explicitly declared dropped.

forbids.why: LAW 1b -- an unreachable reader maps onto no-outcome, NEVER onto clean

5.name: build it  [STRONGEST CAUSATION -- git computes the hash]
5._independent_trace: the git commit hash. A model cannot write a valid hash for a diff that does not exist.

requires.why: the only literally un-forgeable trace in the chain
step 5.6 -- 'a plan that cites nothing did not check anything'
LAW 1b -- the no-outcome member is what keeps 'no tester ran' honest instead of clean. /skill-tester is ruled skipped (the owner 2026-08-07), so NO-TESTER-RAN is the live value.

forbids.why: step 5.10 -- 'an untested skill is never recorded as a passing one'

6.name: the live run and the loop back
6._independent_trace: a FOREIGN session id in arm-events.log. Session A structurally cannot produce it -- it would have to be a different session.

requires.why: the strongest free trace in the system -- the log already records exactly these fields
driver stop-check -- 'an observation that lives only in the transcript is lost'
'the human says it is good enough to stop' is the only clause that can close this phase

forbids.why: if session B is session A, the whole point of the two-window split is gone
